name: C++
summary: Learn modern C++ values, containers, algorithms, references, and resource ownership.

lessons.title: Program entry, values, and streams
lessons.explanation: A C++ program begins at main. Standard library names are in the std namespace. Use auto when the initializer makes its type clear and const when a variable should remain fixed.

api.name: std::cout << value
api.description: Send a formatted value to standard output.

api.name: std::string
api.description: Own an adjustable sequence of characters.

api.name: auto
api.description: Deduce the declared type from an initializer.

lessons.practice: Print a title, unit price, and quantity using explicitly typed values and an inferred total.
lessons.pitfall: Use the matching header for each standard facility you use. Transitive includes are not guaranteed.

lessons.title: Conditions, loops, and functions
lessons.explanation: Use if and else for decisions. A range-for visits values in a range. A function names a reusable operation and specifies a return type.

api.name: std::array<T, N>
api.description: Store a fixed number of elements with value semantics.

api.name: for (auto value : range)
api.description: Visit each element by copying its value.

api.name: break / continue
api.description: Exit the loop or skip the rest of the current iteration.

lessons.practice: Write a function that totals values above a threshold. Use C++17 or newer for std::array deduction in this example.
lessons.pitfall: Integer division discards the fractional part. Convert an operand when you need a fractional result.

lessons.title: Vectors, maps, and checked access
lessons.explanation: Use vector for contiguous resizable data and unordered_map for key-to-value lookup without sorted iteration. Use const references when reading large values without copying them.

api.name: std::vector::push_back()
api.description: Append an element to a growable array.

api.name: std::vector::at(index)
api.description: Check an index and throw std::out_of_range when it is invalid.

api.name: std::unordered_map::find(key)
api.description: Return an iterator to an entry, or end() when absent.

lessons.practice: Count characters in a short word, then print the count of a character without inserting a new key.
lessons.pitfall: Growing a vector may invalidate its iterators, pointers, and references.

lessons.title: References, classes, and invariants
lessons.explanation: A reference is another name for an object. Use a const reference for read-only access. A class can keep its fields private and enforce valid state through its public methods.

api.name: const T&
api.description: Pass an object by reference without permitting mutation through the reference.

api.name: method() const
api.description: Mark a method as read-only for ordinary object fields.

api.name: private
api.description: Restrict access to implementation details.

lessons.practice: Add a decrement method that rejects a negative result.
lessons.pitfall: A reference must not outlive the object it refers to.

lessons.title: Algorithms, iterators, and lambdas
lessons.explanation: Algorithms operate over iterator ranges. The end iterator marks the position after the last element. Use a lambda to supply a short comparison or test.

api.name: std::sort(first, last)
api.description: Sort a range in place.

api.name: std::find(first, last, value)
api.description: Find the first matching value or return last.

api.name: std::count_if(first, last, predicate)
api.description: Count values that pass a test.

lessons.practice: Sort scores in descending order and count the values that fall within an inclusive range.
lessons.pitfall: A sorting comparator must report false for equal inputs. Using >= instead of > violates its ordering requirement.

lessons.title: RAII and ownership with unique_ptr
lessons.explanation: Tie cleanup to the lifetime of an object. Standard containers own their storage and clean it up when they go out of scope. Use unique_ptr when dynamic storage needs one explicit owner.

api.name: std::make_unique<T>(args...)
api.description: Create a dynamically allocated object with an exclusive owner.

api.name: std::unique_ptr<T>
api.description: Release the owned object automatically.

api.name: std::move(value)
api.description: Allow another operation to move from a value. The receiving operation determines what happens.

lessons.practice: Write a function returning a unique_ptr to a populated vector and print its first element.
lessons.pitfall: Prefer an ordinary value or a standard container when dynamic ownership adds no benefit.

lessons.title: Stream input, strings, and optional values
lessons.explanation: Use stream extraction to parse typed values and getline to read a whole line. Use optional when a function can meaningfully return no value.

api.name: std::getline(stream, text)
api.description: Read characters through the next newline or end of stream.

api.name: std::ifstream
api.description: Open a file stream for input and close it automatically.

api.name: std::optional<T>::value_or(fallback)
api.description: Read a value if present or return a fallback.

lessons.practice: Try the parser with an empty string, "42x", and a negative number.
lessons.pitfall: Check a stream operation before using an output variable. Extraction can fail.
